A keyword sweep would report the reserved terms as present and prove nothing, since naming what stays reserved is the join's job. So the test was for the values such tables would contain.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-three attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 282b7097 at 0444, 12710 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All nine cited pins reproduce, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head, artifact and version are both 1, and file08StatusToken is the bare string OPEN matching the live DR-G22 status cell — an attack with extra force here because the DR-126 row join is cited throughout and none of its standing leaked in. The table-population attack was the one worth doing properly. A keyword sweep would report the reserved terms as present and prove nothing, since naming what stays reserved is precisely this join's job, so I tested for the values such tables would hold: zero OS names, zero filesystem names, zero architecture names, no version or build literal, and the three ikconfig mentions all inside the phrase ikconfigParserVectors within refusals. Rosetta appears four times, all refusals or the false summary flag, and appears nowhere in the DR-126 row join, so nothing was imported. The join names the reserved material four times and populates none of it. The two-join structure is handled as well as its DR-G16 counterpart. platform-tcb-leftover-join.v5 is the DR-126 row join and carries the same G22 obligations plus OBL-RESERVED-TABLES; the overlap is disclosed four times including by naming both shared leftovers, and I verified at source that v5 still holds OBL-RESERVED-TABLES and OBL-G22-FX-AUTHORING at leftoverDesign true with DR-126's own OPEN token. Both artifacts hold the shared obligation open, so neither can close while the other appears closed. The pinned version is v5, the latest, with its own ACCEPT 0/0 — an earlier pin would have been wrong because the standing it reports could have moved. The single corpus class is identical four ways and matches the live file 08 harness cell, and it is held as one element at every site: the phrase carries six slash-separated words, and decomposing it would be the error the G16 catalog's slashJoiner exists to prevent. Completeness came back null — G22 v1 names only OBL-G22-HARNESS-SPEC, which is carried, and has no leftoverDesignRemaining enumeration — and its leftoverNameNote independently confirms the four reserved items and TCB v45's CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED standing that the join reproduces. Bookkeeping reconciles at five and five. Recorded rather than raised: DR-G22 is the eleventh row where a harness cell reads 'not authored' while the specification exists, covered by my standing recommendation that the coordinator dispose of the family in one act. Disclosure: all three Claude-lane verdicts this join rests on are my lane's. Having produced two false positives from an unanchored identifier pattern on the previous subject, I used an anchored one here from the start, and I re-read the neighbouring join at source rather than assuming it mirrored the DR-G16 case.
